# llms.txt for ground-rules

> Compile natural-language agent constraints into validated, enforceable policy.

## Install
npm i ground-rules

## What it does
- compileRules(text): deterministic, offline. "Never delete production" becomes a deny rule on delete_*. "Refunds over $500 need approval" becomes require_approval on refund_* with labels {amount_usd_gte:"500"}. "Only read X" becomes allow read_* plus deny update_* and deny delete_*.
- validatePolicy(policy): finds conflicting rules, shadowed (unreachable) rules, and risky shapes like allow on tool "*". Assumes first-match-wins order.
- compileWithModel(text, model): sends a schema-constrained prompt to your LLM, parses JSON, validates, throws on conflicts.

## Quickstart
import { compileRules, validatePolicy } from "ground-rules";
const policy = compileRules("Never touch production without asking.\nRefunds over $500 need approval.");
// policy = { version:"1", default:"deny", rules:[...] }
const report = validatePolicy(policy);
// report = { conflicts:[], unreachable:[], warnings:[] }

## Policy shape (callgate-compatible)
{ version:"1", default:"deny", rules:[{ on:"tool.call", where:{ tool:"read_*", labels:{ env:"production" } }, decide:"allow"|"deny"|"require_approval"|"redact"|"defer"|"escalate"|"simulate", to?:"escalation-target" }] }
Tool matchers are globs: "*" matches all, "read_*" matches read_customer. Labels carry conditions the enforcing gate evaluates (env, amount_usd_gte).

## Limits
- Deterministic compiler covers common phrasings; novel phrasing needs compileWithModel with your own LLM function.
- Label-based numeric conditions (amount_usd_gte) need a gate that evaluates them.
- Validator catches subsumption conflicts, not partial-overlap edge cases.
